mathematical_sources.title: Pure Infinitely Self-Modifying Code is Realizable and Turing-complete

mathematical_sources.note: Cambridge Computer Laboratory (2013), Sections 2-6. MOV simulation uses a static body, four registers and one unconditional loop backedge. It is a foundation rather than a pure-SMC construction. The disclosed mathematical address model returns zero for invalid reads.

mathematical_sources.note: PLDI 2007, 66-77. Context for verification of mutable machine code; its separation-logic system and soundness theorem are not formalized here.
mathematical_sources.title: Certified Self-Modifying Code

mathematical_sources.note: Information Hiding, LNCS 4437, 232-248 (2007). Context for code analysis and obfuscation; its state-enhanced control-flow graph is not the machine model used by the principal formalized theorem.
mathematical_sources.title: A Model for Self-Modifying Code

related_formalizations.note: Cai, Shao and Vaynberg provide an earlier Coq formalization of a logic for general self-modifying code. This development does not use that implementation or claim to replace it; its pure-SMC universality construction is a different result.

Uses the pinned Mathlib computability/Turing-machine development and proves effective finite-machine and TM0 representation bridges. This is a dependency relationship; no claim to be the first formalization of these background notions.
